summaries: Initial full implementation of Time Loop as a Godot 4 project at project root: title screen with rotating overlapping clock hands and the supplied backdrop, chapter menu (4 chapters x 6 levels with locked/unlocked state), 24 procedurally-defined levels with chapter escalation, a 30-second loop with deterministic 30 Hz player recording, ghost replays driven by recorded state, ghost-driven switch/plate/door/laser/enemy interactions, timeline HUD with per-ghost markers, reset, exit-crystal gating, and level-complete metrics (loops used + final-loop exit time). Uses the supplied Art package textures verbatim via res:// paths with nearest filtering and integer scaling; all art remains documented as mock placeholders. Interprets 'up to four loops' as three recorded ghosts plus the current controlled loop, as instructed. Deterministic named scenarios are implemented, with near_rewind and near_victory first. No input traces are fabricated (Player owns demo_outputs).

scenarios.description: Start level 1 with three recorded ghost replays present and the loop clock advanced to 24 seconds so the imminent rewind is exercised quickly.
Start level 1 with one recorded ghost and all required switches held, clock advanced to 12 seconds so the exit crystal is active and completion is one touch away.
Ordinary title screen; normal flow to chapter menu and gameplay.
Chapter 1 level with one active ghost replay for a single-ghost puzzle demonstration.
Chapter 2 level with two active ghost replays exercising layered temporal cooperation.
Chapter 3 level with three active ghosts, plus doors, lasers and enemy distraction.
Loads level 1 already completed so the Level Complete overlay with loops used and exit time is shown.
Level 1 with two ghosts loaded so the reset button can be demonstrated clearing all ghosts.
Chapter 4 four-loop-orchestration level with three active ghosts and the maximum interactable set.

controls: R: reset level and clear all ghosts
Mouse: menu and chapter/level selection, reset button
